To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) segment disclosures are associated with significantly lower abnormal returns around the announcement date than the matched group; (ii) this effect is more pronounced for firms with high segment disclosure scores, and; (iii) this effect is stronger for firms with higher levels of institutional ownership.

(i) segment disclosure has information content in that it enables investors to better predict future earnings; and (ii) this information content is incremental to that provided by the disclosure of earnings per share (EPS), and the disclosure of earnings components (e.g. sales, cost of sales and other operating costs).

(1) firms that voluntarily provide segment disclosures have significantly lower residual returns than a matched sample of firms that do NOT provide such disclosure, and (2) the magnitude of the difference in abnormal returns between the two groups of firms is significantly higher for firms that provide more detailed segment disclosures.
